summary: AI observability is essential for understanding, debugging, and optimizing LLM applications in production, where non-deterministic outputs, latency spikes, and runaway token costs can silently degrade quality and inflate bills. Observability tools provide distributed tracing, evaluation, and cost tracking so teams can catch regressions, measure output quality, and control spend. As LLM apps scale in 2026, these platforms have become core infrastructure rather than optional add-ons.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces of LLM chains and agents, token usage, latency, cost, and evaluation metrics for applications built with or without LangChain.
features: Distributed tracing with span hierarchies and trace-level replay for debugging
Dataset creation and LLM-as-judge evaluations
Prompt playground and prompt versioning
Human annotation queues and feedback collection
Monitoring dashboards for latency, cost, and error rates
tools.pricing: Free Developer tier includes ~5,000 traces/month; Plus plan adds seats and higher volume. Beyond the included allowance, base traces (14-day retention) cost $2.50 per 1k and extended traces (400-day retention) cost $5.00 per 1k. Enterprise pricing is custom.
tools.best_for: Teams building LangChain/LangGraph agents who want tightly integrated tracing, evaluation, and prompt management in one platform.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests and responses, token usage, per-model and per-user costs, latency, caching efficiency, and error rates via a proxy or async logging.
features: One-line proxy integration for request/response logging
Cost and usage dashboards segmented by user, model, and property
Prompt caching and request retries to reduce spend
Rate limiting and user-level budgeting
Sessions and tracing for agent workflows
tools.pricing: Free tier includes up to 10,000 traces/month; Pro at $79/month (approx. $79 per 100,000 traces beyond base); Team at $799/month; custom Enterprise plans.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting fast, low-effort cost tracking and gateway-level controls across any LLM provider via a simple proxy.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: LLM experiments, traces, prompt evaluations, and model performance through W&B Weave, plus broader ML training and experiment tracking.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
Experiment tracking and model/version management
Custom evaluation pipelines and scorers
Rich visualization and reporting dashboards
Integration with the full ML training lifecycle
tools.pricing: Free personal tier; paid plans usage-based with custom Team and Enterprise pricing; typically priced per seat plus data/trace volume.
tools.best_for: ML and research teams that already use W&B for model training and want LLM observability unified with their experiment tracking.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production LLM and ML model performance, including traces, embeddings/drift, hallucination and quality evals, latency, and cost at scale.
features: LLM tracing and evaluation via Arize and open-source Phoenix
Drift, data quality, and performance monitoring
Embedding analysis and clustering for troubleshooting
Online and offline evals with LLM-as-judge
Alerting and dashboards for production monitoring
tools.pricing: Open-source Phoenix is free and self-hostable; Arize AX offers a free tier with paid Pro and custom Enterprise plans.
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing production-grade monitoring, drift detection, and evaluation across both traditional ML and LLM systems.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, nested spans, token usage, cost, latency, prompt versions, and evaluation scores — framework-agnostic and open source.
features: Open-source, self-hostable tracing with span hierarchies
Prompt management and versioning
Evaluations (LLM-as-judge, custom, and user feedback)
Datasets and experiment comparison
Cost and usage analytics dashboards
tools.pricing: Free self-hosted (open source); managed cloud has a free Hobby tier, Core/Pro plans (around $29+/month), and custom Enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, framework-agnostic observability stack they can self-host for data control.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM and vector DB calls instrumented via OpenTelemetry, capturing traces, token usage, latency, and costs exportable to any OTel-compatible backend.
features: Open-source OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation
Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and frameworks
Vendor-neutral export to Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, etc.
Standardized spans for LLM and vector DB operations
Integrates with Traceloop's managed platform
tools.pricing: Free and open source (Apache-licensed); costs depend on the chosen OTel backend. Traceloop's managed offering has free and paid tiers.
tools.best_for: Engineering teams that want standards-based, vendor-neutral LLM telemetry integrated into existing OpenTelemetry observability stacks.

cost_tips: Cache frequent or identical prompts and responses (e.g., with Helicone or provider-native prompt caching) to avoid paying for repeated completions.
Route requests to the cheapest model that meets quality needs — use smaller or distilled models for simple tasks and reserve frontier models for complex reasoning.
Trim token usage by shortening system prompts, truncating context, summarizing history, and setting sensible max_token limits on outputs.
Monitor cost per user, feature, and model with observability dashboards, set budget alerts and rate limits, and batch or deduplicate requests where possible.
